leftEvidence.title: David rescues Keilah and must leave it

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David twice inquires before striking the Philistines, saves Keilah, then learns that its leaders would surrender him and departs into wilderness strongholds.
points.right: Jonathan strengthens David’s hand in God and renews covenant; Ziphites report David, Saul closes in, and a Philistine raid interrupts the pursuit.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places a rescued city cannot become secure refuge inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places David escapes while friendship and external crisis cross Saul’s pursuit inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 23:1–14 and 1 Samuel 23:15–29 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Flight, Covenant, and Restraint” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Covenant strength and a narrowing escape

payload.tension: 1 Samuel 23:1–14 foregrounds a rescued city cannot become secure refuge; 1 Samuel 23:15–29 foregrounds David escapes while friendship and external crisis cross Saul’s pursuit. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
